items.prompt: State why programs must be translated before they can run.
items.canonical_answer: A computer's processor executes only machine code, so a program written in an assembly or a high-level language must be translated into machine code before any of it can run.
marking_guidance: 1 mark: the meaning - the processor executes only machine code, so source must be translated first.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 5.2 claim ledger.

items.prompt: Explain why three different translators exist: an assembler, a compiler and an interpreter.
items.canonical_answer: Each exists for a different kind of source and a different working style: an assembler translates assembly language one mnemonic at a time, because assembly is machine code in readable form; a compiler translates a whole high-level program into machine code before any of it runs, so the result runs on its own; an interpreter translates and executes a high-level program statement by statement at run time, so each edit is tested at once. The source language and the working style name the translator, which is why three exist.
marking_guidance: Reason: each translator serves a different kind of source - assembly, whole-program, statement-by-statement - 1 mark.
Purpose: so the programmer picks the translator that matches the work, because the working style differs between developing and distributing - 1 mark.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 5.2 claim ledger.

items.prompt: A bank's cash machines run a long-finished program that must run fast and be installed on thousands of machines. Explain why a compiler suits this program.
items.canonical_answer: The program is finished, so development speed no longer matters, and it must run at the machine's own speed on machines that never see the source: the compiler produces a machine-code file that runs on its own, without the compiler or the interpreter present, and the source stays private. Installing the compiled file on the thousands of machines is what compiling suits - a finished program for many users.
marking_guidance: Context: this finished program on the given thousands of machines - 1 mark.
Reason: because the compiled file runs on its own at full speed and keeps the source private, compiling suits the finished program, so the choice follows from its stage of life - 1 mark.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 5.2 claim ledger.

items.prompt: Describe two features of an assembler’s work.
items.canonical_answer: It translates one mnemonic at a time, with each assembly instruction becoming one machine instruction, so the translation stays close and exact. It resolves labels through the symbol table, replacing each symbolic address with the numeric address the first pass computed, so the programmer writes names and the assembler writes numbers.
marking_guidance: Features: two points, 1 mark each - the one-to-one translation of mnemonics, and the symbol-table resolution of labels into addresses.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 5.2 claim ledger.

items.prompt: Explain one benefit of using an interpreter during program development.
items.canonical_answer: Each edit is tested immediately: the interpreter translates and executes statement by statement, with no compile step between the edit and the result, and when a statement is wrong the interpreter stops there and reports it, so the programmer fixes it at once. The development loop shrinks to edit-and-run, which is the interpreter’s gift to development.
marking_guidance: Benefit: the edit-and-run loop with no compile step - 1 mark.
Because the interpreter stops at a statement’s error and reports it, the fix happens at once, so development moves quickly - 1 mark.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 5.2 claim ledger.

items.prompt: Explain one drawback of distributing a program as interpreted source.
items.canonical_answer: Wherever the program runs, the interpreter must be present, and the statement-by-statement translation costs time on every run, so the program runs slower than compiled code. The readable source travels with the program too, so whoever receives it can read it, which is the cost of shipping interpreted.
marking_guidance: Drawback: the interpreter must be present and the run is slower - 1 mark.
Because the translation happens during the run and the source travels with the program, each run pays the cost and the code is readable by its recipients - 1 mark.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 5.2 claim ledger.

items.prompt: A student is writing a small game, changing it daily; a firm has finished its payroll program and will install it on fifty machines. Explain which translator each should use, and why.
items.canonical_answer: The student should use an interpreter: daily changes want the edit-and-run loop, the interpreter stops at each error for immediate fixing, and the game’s speed matters less than the pace of development. The firm should use a compiler: the payroll program is finished, it must run at full speed on fifty machines, and the firm’s source stays private while only the compiled files are installed. Each choice follows from where each program is in its life - developing or finished - which is the justification.
marking_guidance: Suitable choices named for both programs - 1 mark for the student’s interpreter, because the edit-and-run loop suits daily changes.
Reason for the firm: the compiler’s file runs at full speed without the source, so the fifty installed machines are served - 1 mark.
Context: the justification is developed in this scenario - the stage of each program’s life is what decides it - 1 mark.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 5.2 claim ledger.

items.prompt: A weather station's control program runs for years on one small controller and must use the processor's time exactly. Explain why it may be written in assembly language and translated with an assembler.
items.canonical_answer: Exact use of the processor's time needs exact control of the machine instructions, and assembly gives that: each mnemonic is one machine instruction, so the programmer controls every instruction the processor will execute, with nothing added between the writing and the running. The assembler turns the mnemonics into machine code one for one, which is why timing-exact programs are written in assembly and assembled.
marking_guidance: Context: this controller with its given timing need - 1 mark.
Reason: because each mnemonic is one machine instruction, the programmer controls the exact instruction stream, so the timing is the code’s own timing - 1 mark.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 5.2 claim ledger.

items.prompt: A learner writes that an interpreter fixes errors as it meets them. Explain the error.
items.canonical_answer: An interpreter stops at an error so the programmer can fix it; it does not fix anything. The interpreter reports where the statement failed, and the correction is the programmer’s work. The test: software reports errors; people correct them.
marking_guidance: 1 mark: the error named - the interpreter has been given the correcting power, when it only stops and reports.
1 mark: the correction with the test - the interpreter halts at the failing statement for the programmer to fix, because software reports errors and people correct them.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 5.2 claim ledger.

items.prompt: State what a compiler does.
items.canonical_answer: A compiler translates a whole high-level language program into machine code before the program runs, producing a machine-code file that runs on its own.
marking_guidance: 1 mark: the meaning - whole-program translation into machine code, done before the run, producing a standalone file.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 5.2 claim ledger.

items.prompt: Describe two features of a compiled program.
items.canonical_answer: It runs without the compiler or the source present, at the machine’s own speed, because the translation was finished before the run began. Its file is built for one type of machine, so running it on a different type needs a recompilation, and each change to the program needs a new compile before the change can be tested.
marking_guidance: Features: two points, 1 mark each - the standalone run at full speed, and the single-machine build with recompilation for changes and other machines.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 5.2 claim ledger.

items.prompt: Explain why a program under daily development is run with an interpreter rather than a compiler.
items.canonical_answer: Daily development is edit-and-run, and the interpreter fits the loop: no compile step stands between the edit and the test, and an error stops the run at the statement where it is, so it is found at once. A compiler would demand a full recompilation for every change, however small, which turns each test into a wait, so the interpreter is the development translator.
marking_guidance: Reason: the interpreter tests each edit at once, with no compile step - 1 mark.
Purpose: so small changes stay cheap to try, because a compiler’s recompilation would put a wait inside every loop of the day - 1 mark.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 5.2 claim ledger.

items.prompt: Describe the difference between a compiler and an interpreter.
items.canonical_answer: A compiler translates the whole program into machine code before any of it runs, producing a file that runs on its own, whereas an interpreter translates and executes statement by statement at run time, needing the interpreter present and running slower. The compiler is a before-the-fact translator for finished programs, whereas the interpreter is an at-the-fact translator for development and small runs.
marking_guidance: Difference: whole-program-before against statement-by-statement-at-run-time - 1 mark per side, and both sides are needed with what each produces and needs.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 5.2 claim ledger.

items.prompt: State what is meant by a language being partly compiled and partly interpreted.
items.canonical_answer: The source is first compiled into an intermediate code, and that intermediate code is then executed by a matching interpreter at run time, so part of the translation is done in advance and the rest at run time.
marking_guidance: 1 mark: the meaning - compiled to an intermediate code, then interpreted at run time.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 5.2 claim ledger.

items.prompt: Explain why a language may be designed to be partly compiled and partly interpreted.
items.canonical_answer: The compile step does the whole-program work once - parsing and checking - and produces a compact intermediate code, while the interpreter does the run-time work on any machine that has the matching interpreter. The arrangement buys a share of the compiler’s speed and a share of the interpreter’s portability, so programs run reasonably fast without a separate compilation for every machine type.
marking_guidance: Reason: the compile step does the once-only work and the interpreter does the run-time work - 1 mark.
Purpose: so the language gains speed and portability together, because one intermediate file runs wherever the matching interpreter exists - 1 mark.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 5.2 claim ledger.

items.prompt: Describe two benefits of the intermediate-code arrangement for distributing a program.
items.canonical_answer: One intermediate file runs on any machine that has the matching interpreter, so the distributor ships one file instead of a separate compilation for each machine type. The intermediate code is not the source, so the readable source stays private, while the file still starts quickly because the parsing was done at compile time.
marking_guidance: Features: two benefits as two points, 1 mark each - one file for every machine with the interpreter, and a private source with quick starts.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 5.2 claim ledger.

items.prompt: State what an IDE is.
items.canonical_answer: An Integrated Development Environment is a program that brings the tools of development into one place: an editor to write the code, translators to build it, and debugging tools to find its faults.
marking_guidance: 1 mark: the meaning - one program carrying the editor, translators and debugging tools together.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 5.2 claim ledger.

items.prompt: Describe two features found in an IDE for coding.
items.canonical_answer: Context-sensitive prompts suggest what can be written at the current point in a statement, so the editor answers as the programmer types. Auto-completion finishes the word being typed from the available names, so less is typed and names are spelled right the first time.
marking_guidance: Features: two points, 1 mark each - the prompt that suggests what comes next, and the auto-completion that finishes the word.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 5.2 claim ledger.

The table shows IDE features. Complete the four missing entries.

| IDE feature | What it does |
|---|---|
| (a) | Flags syntax errors as the code is typed |
| Single stepping | (b) |
| (c) | Displays chosen variables’ values as the program runs |
| Prettyprint | (d) |
items.canonical_answer: (a) Dynamic syntax checking. (b) Executes one statement at a time, so the programmer follows the run closely. (c) A variable watch window. (d) Presents code with consistent layout, keeping a long program readable.
marking_guidance: Context: this IDE’s features as given - 1 mark per completed entry, (a), (b), (c), (d).
Reason: each entry names the feature from its job, because suggesting, checking, stopping, showing and laying out are different jobs, so the four entries carry 4 marks.

items.prompt: A learner writes that context-sensitive prompts, dynamic syntax checking and auto-completion are one feature of an IDE. Explain the error.
items.canonical_answer: They are three separate features, each doing a different thing: a context-sensitive prompt suggests what can come next, dynamic syntax checking flags errors as the code is typed, and auto-completion finishes the word being typed. The test: is it suggesting, checking, or finishing? Each answer names a different feature.
marking_guidance: 1 mark: the error named - the three features have been rolled into one, a confusion of suggesting, checking and finishing.
1 mark: the correction with the test - each feature is named by its job, because suggesting, checking and finishing are three different jobs.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 5.2 claim ledger.

items.prompt: Asked to name two debugging tools in an IDE, a learner names context-sensitive prompts and prettyprint. Explain the error.
items.canonical_answer: Prompts and prettyprint help write and present code, not find faults in running code. The debugging tools are the ones that work on the running program: breakpoints, where execution pauses; single stepping, one statement at a time; and variable watch windows, showing chosen values as they change. The test: does the feature help find a fault in running code? Then it is a debugging tool.
marking_guidance: 1 mark: the error named - coding and presentation tools have been given for debugging tools, a confusion of writing with fault-finding.
1 mark: the correction with the test - breakpoints, single stepping and watch windows work on the running program, because finding a fault in running code is what a debugging tool does.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 5.2 claim ledger.

items.prompt: Explain why breakpoints and watch windows are used together in debugging.
items.canonical_answer: A breakpoint pauses the run at a chosen statement, so the programmer can inspect the program’s state there instead of printing it out, and a watch window shows the chosen variables’ values at that moment and as the stepping continues. Together they turn a fault into something seen: where the program stops is where the suspicion is, and what the watched values do there is the evidence, which is why the two are used together.
marking_guidance: Reason: the breakpoint stops the run at the suspicious statement - 1 mark.
Purpose: so the watch window shows what the variables believed at that point, because the stop and the show together turn a fault into evidence - 1 mark.
items.provenance: Authored for 9618 AS from the topic 5.2 claim ledger.

items.prompt:
A youth centre in Katutura is building a booking program. One volunteer edits and tests it each afternoon; the centre also has a finished enrolment program that must run at full speed on the front desk’s older computer.
(a) Explain which translator each program should use, and why. [4]
(b) The volunteers write the booking program in an IDE. Explain how two IDE features help them while writing the code, and two while debugging it. [4]
items.canonical_answer:
(a) The booking program is under daily development, so it should be run with an interpreter: each edit is tested immediately with no compile step, and an error stops the run at its statement so the fix happens at once - the interpreter stops, the volunteer fixes. The enrolment program is finished and must run at full speed on one older machine, so it should be compiled: the compiled file runs on its own at the machine’s own speed, without an interpreter present, and the centre’s source stays private.
(b) While writing: context-sensitive prompts suggest what can come next at the current point, and auto-completion finishes the word being typed, so names are spelled right the first time. While debugging: single stepping executes one statement at a time so the run can be followed, and a variable watch window shows the chosen values as they change, so a fault becomes something seen.
marking_guidance: Part (a): the reason each program gets its translator - 4 marks, 1 per point: the interpreter for the daily edits, the stop-and-fix at errors, the compiled standalone speed, the private source.

Part (b): the context of this given IDE - 4 points: one coding feature with its job (prompts or auto-completion), the second coding feature, and two debugging features (stepping, watch window) with what each shows.

context.situation: A youth centre develops one program and runs another finished one.

items.prompt:
The table shows three translators and their properties. Read the table and complete the four missing entries, then answer the question.

| Translator | When it translates | What is produced |
|---|---|---|
| Assembler | (a) | (b) |
| Interpreter | (c) | Statement-by-statement execution at run time |
| Compiler | The whole program, before it runs | (d) |

items.canonical_answer:
(a) The whole assembly program, before it runs, in two passes. (b) Machine code, one machine instruction per assembly instruction. (c) At run time, statement by statement. (d) A machine-code file that runs on its own, without the compiler present.
(e) The interpreter: it translates each statement as the program runs, so the interpreter must be present wherever the program runs, because the translation happens during the run.

Answer and value: (e) the interpreter - 1 mark - because its translation happens at run time, the interpreter must be present - 1 mark.
The completed table shows the three translators separated by timing, because when the translation happens is what tells them apart.
